description: E2a's Envelope rack prefab, built from the same primitives its generator uses (SE16/scripts/build-prefabs.py). The prefab is deliberately an envelope AND a VCA -- a bare ADSR emits control voltage and has no audio path, so oscillator->envelope->output would render silence however correct each part was (docs/e2a-prefabs.md 9.3). This case locks that audio path and the two pin defaults V1 depends on: ADSR Overall Level at 1 so the VCA is unity gain rather than x10 into clipping, and the GATE jack open at 10 so a three-module rack with nothing to patch a gate from still sounds. The IN jack is driven by --set-pin rather than a cable, standing in for the oscillator a rack would patch into it -- so the recording is the envelope contour itself, with no oscillator phase drift in it, which is why this case needs no relaxed gates. A patch point carries VOLTS, and 10 V is full scale: the 5 V here is what the Oscillator prefab actually delivers (measured 0.49 = 4.9 V), and it is why the reference peaks at 0.5 rather than 1.0. Set it to 1 and the whole reference drops 14 dB, which looks like a gain regression and is not one. Keep this case's script in step with the Envelope entry in PREFABS in build-prefabs.py. REFERENCE SEEDED ON macOS, 2026-08-18 -- unlike the other two, which came from Linux. CI is Linux, so the first CI run is this reference's first cross-platform comparison; a null-test failure there is more likely to be platform drift than a regression, and E1a's numbers are the yardstick for telling them apart.
